questions.q: What basic instance pattern did Platform Fundamentals already introduce, and what does this lesson build on top of it?
options: A pattern that has nothing to do with this lesson's content
Development, Test/QA, and Production, with deliberate promotion between them — this lesson adds real-world structure beyond those three tiers
A single shared instance for everything, which this lesson replaces entirely
Production only, with Dev and Test added for the first time in this lesson
questions.explain: The three-tier Dev/Test/Prod pattern is the recap; this lesson goes deeper into patterns organizations add around it.

questions.q: What problem does a dedicated Build instance between Dev and Test solve?
options: It stores anonymized data permanently with no other function
It is only used for hosting live Production traffic
It replaces the need for a Test/QA instance entirely
It catches integration problems when multiple developers' changes are merged and run together, before formal Test/QA validation
questions.explain: Build isolates "does this work together at all" from "does this work correctly for a business tester," which are different questions.

questions.q: Why do sub-production instances typically get refreshed from Production periodically?
options: Because their data and configuration otherwise drift away from what Production actually looks like over time
Because Dev and Test instances cannot hold any data at all without a refresh
Because refreshing is required to rename an instance's URL
Because ServiceNow requires a refresh before any upgrade can occur
questions.explain: A clone refresh keeps Dev/Test realistic by replacing a stale snapshot with a recent copy of Production's actual data.

questions.q: What does a Production clone refresh copy into sub-production instances by default?
options: Only configuration changes, never any data records
Nothing; a clone refresh never copies any data at all
Everything — including every real customer's real PII, such as names and email addresses
Only anonymized, fake data with no real customer information
questions.explain: A clone refresh copies everything from Production, including real PII, unless anonymization is applied afterward.

questions.q: Why does a quarterly clone refresh create an operational need for data anonymization?
options: Because anonymization is what makes a clone refresh possible in the first place
Because the clone would otherwise leave real customer PII sitting in Dev and Test, which have no legitimate business need to hold it
It doesn't — anonymization is unrelated to clone refreshes
Because anonymization is required to make the clone process run faster
questions.explain: Applying anonymization right after the clone turns "we copied real PII into Dev" into "Dev never actually held real PII," by design.
